name: ドン・キホーテ六本木店
kind: ディスカウントストア
hoursEn: Open 24 hours (as listed for this store; check before you go)

door.t: 驚安の殿堂 ドン・キホーテ
door.en: The Palace of Amazing Bargains, Don Quijote
door.n: 驚安 (きょうやす) is Don Quijote's own word: 驚く (おどろく, to be amazed) + 安い (やすい, cheap). 殿堂 (でんどう) is a palace or hall. Everyone calls the chain ドンキ.

enter: Walk in through the front doors.

sweets.n: お菓子 (おかし) covers sweets, snacks and crisps. The aisle by the door is full of Kit Kat flavors you only find in Japan.

souvenirs.n: お土産 (おみやげ) are gifts you bring back from a trip: snacks, chopsticks, character goods. 人気 (にんき) means popular.

cosmetics.n: 化粧品 (けしょうひん): make-up and skin care. 日焼け止め (ひやけどめ) is sunscreen, 美容 (びよう) is beauty.

medicine.n: 医薬品 (いやくひん) is medicine; 薬 (くすり) on its own is the everyday word. 風邪薬 (かぜぐすり) is cold medicine.

daily.n: 日用品 (にちようひん): things you use every day, like toothbrushes, tissues and detergent.

drinks.n: お酒 (おさけ) means alcohol in general (and sake). 飲料 (いんりょう) is drinks; 飲み物 (のみもの) in everyday speech.

party.n: Costumes and party goods: Roppongi's Donki is famous for Halloween costumes. コスプレ is cosplay.

register.n: レジ (from register) is the checkout. 袋はご利用ですか？ (ふくろはごりようですか): do you need a bag? 大丈夫です means no thanks.

taxfree.n: 免税 (めんぜい) means tax-free: visitors with a passport can skip the consumption tax (消費税, しょうひぜい) on purchases over ¥5,000.

exit.n: 出口 (でぐち) is exit and 入口 (いりぐち) is entrance: 出る (でる) to go out, 入る (はいる) to go in, 口 (くち) mouth.

escalator.n: 上り (のぼり) is up and 下り (くだり) is down. The upper floors are closed for now: only the ground floor is in the game.

pop.n: The handwritten yellow price cards are called POP (ポップ). 大特価 (だいとっか) is a big sale price, 数量限定 (すうりょうげんてい) means while stocks last.
